title: Derivation of the Thiele equation for magnetic skyrmions using the Mori-Zwanzig formalism
abstract: We use the Mori-Zwanzig formalism to derive an exact generalized Langevin equation governing the dynamics of magnetic skyrmions. Using standard approximations, this generalized Langevin equation is found to reduce to the usual Thiele equation. Our approach provides a general route for obtaining extensions of the Thiele equation applicable to magnetic textures and degrees of freedom not covered by the standard derivation route. It also provides some insights into the microscopic justification of the standard Thiele equation, specifically concerning contributions of fast modes to the form of the drift and diffusion terms in the Fokker-Planck equation for skyrmions.
summary: This work uses the advanced Mori-Zwanzig formalism to derive a generalized Langevin equation for magnetic skyrmion dynamics from the stochastic LLG equation. It successfully generalizes the standard Thiele equation by providing a rigorous framework that accounts for complex dynamics beyond simple rigid translations. This offers a powerful theoretical tool for studying magnetic textures in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive an exact generalized Langevin equation governing the dynamics of magnetic skyrmions, starting from the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
main_result: The derived equation is a substantial generalization of the standard Thiele equation, providing a general route for describing the dynamics of magnetic textures beyond the standard rigid translation assumption.
method: The core method is the Mori-Zwanzig projection operator formalism applied to the stochastic dynamics, leading to a generalized Fokker-Planck equation for the skyrmion position probability density.
model_or_system: The system under study is magnetic skyrmions, which are particle-like spin textures in magnetic materials. The dynamics are modeled using the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.

important_parameters: The derivation is sensitive to the assumption of finite area for the skyrmion and the approximations made regarding fast modes and memory kernels.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include the Markovian approximation for the memory kernel and, ultimately, making physical assumptions (like rigid translation) to reconcile the general formalism with known results.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the derivation involves equations for the generalized Fokker-Planck equation, the resulting equation of motion, and the final Langevin equation.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the stochastic dynamics via the LLG equation, applying the Mori-Zwanzig formalism to project the dynamics onto the slow variables (skyrmion position), and then deriving the generalized Fokker-Planck equation, culminating in the comparison and reduction to the Thiele equation.
why_interesting: The use of the Mori-Zwanzig formalism to derive transport equations for extended objects like skyrmions provides a rigorous, general theoretical framework for non-equilibrium dynamics, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems and many-body dynamics.
